Maya (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — during canary this morning I saw a p95 latency spike for llama3-pool on the short-chat route. p95 jumped from ~45ms -> ~210ms around 09:12 UTC.
Sam (mlops): ack. any correlated deploys or config changes?
Maya (eng-runtime): we rolled a batch-slicer throttle tweak + heartbeat change to KV prefetch (kv.heartbeat_ms: 50 -> 200) as part of the canary. no model or kernel changes.
Tony (perf): that heartbeat bump can cause more concurrent prefetch jobs which in turn increases KV miss churn and kernel selector thrashing. can you capture a flamegraph?
Maya (eng-runtime): pasted short perf dump here from one affected host:
```
# top lines from async profile
3.2s  kernel_selector.evaluate()
2.6s  kv.prefetch_task()
1.9s  batch_slicer.wait_for_token_budget()
0.9s  kv.populate_cache()
```
Sam (mlops): interesting — kernel_selector.evaluate being top suggests rapid kernel switching decisions under load. what's the selector strategy?
Maya (eng-runtime): default: `selector: cost_weighted` on the route. the canary config changed `batch_slicer.max_batch_tokens` from 1024 to 2048 and increased `kv.heartbeat_ms` to reduce missed prefixes.
perf-bot: ALERT: route=short-chat, model=llama3-13b, p95_latency=210ms, kv_miss_rate=68% (baseline 18%).
Tony (perf): kv_miss_rate jump to 68% is the smoking gun. higher miss rate => more backend fetches and kernel reconfigs. also saw increased small-batch count leading to suboptimal kernels.
Elena (eng-sre): do we have token distribution samples? short-chat templates usually have prefix length 48-64, so doubling max_batch_tokens could change batching behavior.
Maya (eng-runtime): attached a sample histogram: most requests are 12-80 tokens; very few >512. doubling the max batch size allowed longer waits and more prefetches to run concurrently.
Sam (mlops): action idea: revert kv.heartbeat to 50ms, set batch_slicer.max_batch_tokens back to 1024, and flip selector to `latency_first` for short-chat route. run A/B for 10 minutes.
Tony (perf): +1. also suggest enabling `kv.prefetch_limit_per_host: 1` to avoid prefetch storm. small config snippet for experiment:
```json
{
  "route": "short-chat",
  "model": "llama3-13b",
  "selector": "latency_first",
  "batch_slicer": { "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "delay_ms": 4 },
  "kv": { "heartbeat_ms": 50, "prefetch_limit_per_host": 1 }
}
```
Maya (eng-runtime): queued the rollback for canary config and will start the A/B with `selector=latency_first`. scheduling window 09:30-09:45 UTC.
Elena (eng-sre): if that doesn't fix it, we should capture a full trace with `kernel_selection.debug=true` and sample a couple of failed requests. good to have an automatic fallback policy to pin to a stable kernel when selector churn > threshold.
Sam (mlops): logging note: add `kv.miss_rate` and `kernel_switch_rate` to route dashboard, p95 tail and 99th as well.
Maya (eng-runtime): agree. quick follow-up numbers after rollback (09:34 UTC): p95 down to 52ms, kv_miss_rate 20%, kernel_switch_rate back to baseline. keeping the A/B to validate.
Tony (perf): nice. follow-up experiments to run in the next week: 1) measure impact of `rmsnorm=false` + `silu=true` kernel variants on latency for small batches, 2) profile rope_theta scaling sensitivity with our short-chat template (prefix-heavy).
Maya (eng-runtime): noted. also want to test `kv.prefetch_policy: prefix_only` vs `aggressive` — guessed aggressive was the culprit.
Sam (mlops): can we add a lightweight smoke test harness that simulates prefix-heavy short chats and runs selector stress to expose kernel thrash before rolling configs? would save a lot of canary grief.
Elena (eng-sre): I'll add a test job in the canary pipeline to run the harness for 2 minutes post-deploy, fail the deploy if kernel_switch_rate spike > 3x baseline.
Maya (eng-runtime): thanks team. next steps: roll back canary (done), run A/B with the JSON config Tony posted, add `kernel_selection.debug` trace if we see instability, and add the harness to canary pipeline.
perf-bot: NOTE: incident closed — rollback restored p95 to acceptable range. :white_check_mark:
Maya (eng-runtime): closing thread, will open a perf doc with the full traces and recommended defaults for short-chat routes (include `selector=latency_first`, `kv.heartbeat_ms=50`, `prefetch_limit_per_host=1`, `batch_slicer.max_batch_tokens=1024`).
Sam (mlops): thanks — please add test vectors and the smoke script path when you post the doc.
Tony (perf): saved the flamegraphs and will attach to the doc.
Maya (eng-runtime): will do, thanks all. :rocket:
